articles.title: Silence of the Lambs moth found in Portchester school compost
articles.summary: The giant African death's-head hawkmoth has a distinctive skull-like marking.
articles.body:
A giant moth made famous by the film poster for Silence of the Lambs has been found in a school compost bin.

The African death's-head hawkmoth was discovered in a nature area at Wicor Primary School in Portchester, Hampshire.

Native to southern Europe and Africa, the moth has a wingspan of up to 14cm and a distinctive skull-like marking on the back of its head.

The species is rarely seen in the UK and the school's horticulturalist Louise Moreton said it was a "once-in-a-lifetime" chance for the children and staff to see it.

More stories from Hampshire & the Isle of Wight

Listen to the latest news from Hampshire and the Isle of Wight

She described how she first noticed it when she heard its distinctive mouse-like squeak.

"It was so loud and so big, I thought 'my goodness we've got another mouse', but no, it was the beautiful moth," she said.

"It looks incredible with its marking like a bee on its underside and it has a very big face as well."

The moth is in a specialist habitat frame in the compost bin, and the school plans to show it to the children before it is released.

"We want the children to share in this - it's a once-in-a-lifetime chance," Moreton said.

"They'll understand its about looking after the wildlife they've brought in to their habitat."

Butterfly Conservation's head of science Prof Richard Fox said it was "always exciting" to spot the species in the UK.

He said the caterpillars, which can be found on potato plants, cannot survive British winters.

"As an uncommon visitor from warmer parts of Europe, it's not your everyday back garden moth, but it can breed here during the summer," he added.

The moth featured in Silence of the Lambs when serial killer Buffalo Bill left it in the mouth of a victim.

It was famously used in the publicity images for the 1991 Oscar-winning film, with its open wings covering Jodie Foster's mouth.

articles.title: Wrexham couple spent £23,000 on fertility treatment but now embryos will be destroyed
articles.summary: Nat and Nik Fraser-Edwards want a change in the law so once an embryo has been made, a donor can't withdraw consent.
articles.body:
Nat and Nik Fraser-Edwards celebrated their son Jude's first birthday last month.

After rounds of failed fertility treatment, Jude was a dream come true for the couple who said they hoped to give him a brother or sister next year. But now their dreams have come "crashing down".

Their sperm donor has withdrawn his consent for further use, and the remaining five embryos in storage will be destroyed after paying £23,000 on fertility treatment.

In the UK, a sperm or egg donor can withdraw consent up until the embryo is transferred into the womb.

The couple now want the law changed so that once an embryo has been created, consent cannot be withdrawn.

The UK government said it sympathised and added it is "keeping all aspects of the regulatory regime under review".

When they returned from their honeymoon in 2023, the couple from north Wales started fertility treatment.

They took out loans and went through rounds of failed fertility treatment in a journey that cost them a total of £23,000.

"There was a lot of pain during that time, and everyone around us seemed to be getting pregnant," recalled Nat, 37.

"All you see is babies. It's not just wanting that baby so much, it's the cancelled plans in case you get that smiley face."

It was only when they turned to a different type of treatment, called ICSI , where the egg is fertilised with sperm and the embryo is created outside of the body, that they had success.

Nat and Nik ended up with six embryos and in August last year, Jude was born.

The embryos were put into storage until the couple were ready to grow their family.

It was during a telephone consultation in June that they found out their embryos would be destroyed.

"It was very much, 'unfortunately your donor has withdrawn his consent to use your embryos'," said Nat, who lives in Penyffordd, near Wrexham.

"They said, 'we keep them for a cooling off period of a year and' - I think the hardest word for us was - 'we then allow them to perish'.

Nik said the couple felt "blindsided" by the fact that their sperm donor could withdraw consent at that stage.

"Yes, we'd signed something," she added. "But we didn't ever recall it being verbally said."

The number of donors in the UK that withdraw consent is unknown as the data isn't collected. While it is rare, it is not unheard of.

Sam Beesley and Carly Estlick are expecting their first child, a boy they plan to call Finn, in October after going through IVF.

"I've been someone who knew from a young age that my job in life was to be a mother," said Sam, 41.

Just like Nat and Nik, Sam and Carly were told last month that their sperm donor had withdrawn consent and their 10 remaining embryos will be destroyed next year.

"When we got the letter saying he had withdrawn consent, it felt like the wind was taken out of our sails," said Sam from Shrewsbury.

"We had been so focussed on the pregnancy and something going wrong, I don't think it's really sunk in yet.

"Carly is already grieving. In her head, they've already been destroyed. Whereas until that day in 2027, I will not stop fighting."

Sam said the news has put pressure on their current pregnancy.

"Carly is very fearful that something will happen to Finn," she said. "It has crossed my mind.

"I did have some reduced movements the other day and had to go to hospital. You can't help thinking, is this going to be ripped away from us as well?

"This is probably our only shot at being parents. I don't know how we could afford to go through it again financially, emotionally, physically."

For both couples, fertility treatment has had an emotional and financial impact.

Nat and Nik say they would have paid anything to have a family, but that the total £23,000 bill means that they did have to make "sacrifices".

"We lived on the breadline for quite a while, just to make this work," Nat said.

"Taking out a loan in order to pay the excessive bill."

Nat and Nik also say they can't afford to go through treatment again, and, for Nik, this means she may never get to experience pregnancy.

"I think, as a woman, it's an amazing thing to be able to do and I didn't want to have any regrets later in life," said Nik, 36.

"We knew we were going to have a sibling for Jude. I think the tables turned a little bit watching Nat go through that experience and I was thinking, 'yeah I'd love to do that'."

The UK fertility regulator HFEA has said that any change in the law on sperm donation is down to the UK government.

"It's about each person who provides an egg or sperm having that autonomy to consent and make that decision to whether they're happy for a child to be born in treatment," said Rachel Cutting, HFEA's director of compliance.

"Once the embryos in the uterus, in the woman's womb, there can't be a withdrawal of consent for that.

"The way that the law is written is that consent can be withdrawn from up to that point.

"We can look at it further, but it is for the law to be changed and that's not something within the power that the HFEA has. We can't change the law. But we are sympathetic to cases like this."

The HFEA has said it is important that clinics warn patients of the possibility of donors withdrawing consent "because it is really upsetting and distressing when this happens".

The UK government said it also sympathises with "anyone facing difficult and distressing circumstances during fertility treatment."

A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson said: "We continue to work closely with the fertility sector to support high-quality, compassionate care, and we keep all aspects of the regulatory regime under review to the same end."

If you or someone you know has been affected by the issues raised in this story, information about available help and support can be found via BBC Action Line .

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: 'Farage faces Met inquiry' and 'Ready for departure?'
articles.summary: Thursday's front pages are dominated by a police investigation into Reform UK and UK airport chaos.
articles.body:
The Financial Times says the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic declined to submit its latest test models to Britain's AI Security Institute. Its report notes that vetted US bodies were given access, prompting alarm in Whitehall. The Daily Star focuses on the comments from Jacob Coxon , a former employee of the company, who warned the technology could kill all humans by the end of the decade. In a nod to the sci-fi movie, The Terminator, its headline reads "Hasta la vista".

The Daily Telegraph focuses on what it calls Labour's "new tax assault on hospitality" - with mayors in England being given the power to impose unlimited levies on tourists. The paper says senior figures in the sector were surprised by the announcement, having initially believed the tax would be capped. One unnamed source is quoted as saying the plans will create a "jobs bloodbath".

The police inquiry into Reform UK leads the Guardian and the Daily Mirror. The Guardian says the financial scandal has deepened - noting that the investigation will form part of an existing inquiry into Reform's political funding. "Farage faces cop quiz on donors," reads the Mirror's headline. The party calls that "pure speculation" in the i Paper.

The Daily Mail says Labour has been branded the "welfare party" by the Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch after the prime minister said he would never prioritise defence spending over benefits. The report calls it a "staggering admission". Writing in the paper, Badenoch says Andy Burnham said "the quiet part out loud". In a similar vein, the Telegraph says Burnham "let the cat out of the bag" .

The Metro leads on the problems at air traffic control and calls for the head of National Air Traffic Services (Nats) to step down with its headline: "Ready for departure?" Its front page features a picture of Martin Rolfe, as well as stranded passengers sleeping at Heathrow airport.

The Duke of Sussex and King Charles III have spoken since Prince Harry returned to the UK with his family, according to the Daily Express . It quotes royal sources who say that, despite conflicting reports, father and son spoke to each other in the first week of the latter's arrival in the Cotswolds.

images.caption: A criminal investigation into Reform UK over allegations it broke foreign funding laws is leading many of Thursday's front pages. The Metropolitan Police is carrying out the inquiry following a broadcast by Channel 4 News last week in which an undercover reporter recorded two senior Reform aides apparently suggesting a way around electoral law to secure foreign party donations. A Reform UK spokesman says the party "denies any wrongdoing and will fully cooperate with the investigation".

articles.title: Trump diz que guerra com Irã acabará após eleição de meio de mandato | G1
articles.standfirst: Declaração ocorre em meio à escalada dos ataques no Golfo e a alertas de assessores de que a guerra pode seguir até o fim de seu governo.
articles.summary: Declaração ocorre em meio à escalada dos ataques no Golfo e a alertas de assessores de que a guerra pode seguir até o fim de seu governo.
articles.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, participa da Convenção Nacional Republicana de Meio de Mandato em Dallas, Texas, EUA, em 9 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Brian Snyder / Reuters

O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump, afirmou nesta quarta-feira (9) que espera que a guerra contra o Irã termine logo após as eleições legislativas de novembro e voltou a ameaçar um ataque à chamada Montanha Pickaxe, área fortificada ligada ao programa nuclear iraniano.

A declaração foi feita durante uma convenção do Partido Republicano. Segundo Trump, Teerã estaria tentando influenciar o resultado das eleições de meio de mandato, que definirão se os republicanos manterão o controle do Congresso americano.

"Acho que a guerra vai acabar imediatamente após a eleição porque eles não conseguem resistir por muito mais tempo. Estão desesperados para tentar influenciar a eleição", disse o presidente a jornalistas.

Trump também afirmou que os Estados Unidos podem atacar a Montanha Pickaxe, um complexo de túneis subterrâneos próximo à instalação de enriquecimento de urânio de Natanz, considerada uma das estruturas mais protegidas do programa nuclear iraniano.

"Estamos observando alguma atividade em Pickaxe. Eu aconselharia o Irã a não tentar ser esperto, porque teremos de atacar com muita força", declarou o republicano.

A ameaça ocorre em meio à maior escalada de ataques contra navios desde o início do conflito entre Estados Unidos e Irã, há seis meses. Na quarta-feira, o governo iraniano afirmou ter atacado dez embarcações próximas ao Estreito de Ormuz após os Estados Unidos afundarem cinco petroleiros iranianos.

As hostilidades reacenderam preocupações sobre o abastecimento global de energia. O petróleo Brent permaneceu acima de US$ 100 por barril nesta quinta-feira (10), enquanto o tráfego marítimo segue afetado tanto no Estreito de Ormuz quanto no Mar Vermelho.

Dados preliminares de rastreamento de navios indicam que apenas sete embarcações atravessaram o Estreito de Ormuz na quarta-feira, cerca de metade da média registrada nos dez dias anteriores.

Assessores acreditam em conflito mais longo

As declarações de Trump contrastam com avaliações feitas dentro da própria Casa Branca. Segundo o jornal Wall Street Journal, os principais assessores do presidente, incluindo o vice-presidente JD Vance e o secretário de Estado Marco Rubio, alertaram reservadamente que a guerra pode durar até o fim do mandato de Trump, em janeiro de 2029.

De acordo com a publicação, autoridades disseram ao presidente, durante reuniões no Salão Oval e na Sala de Situação, que o Irã pode continuar resistindo à pressão militar e econômica americana por vários anos, prolongando o conflito para além da posse do próximo presidente dos EUA.

Ainda segundo o jornal, integrantes do governo discutem internamente a possibilidade de uma guerra prolongada. O Wall Street Journal também informou que o Pentágono já estendeu parte da presença de tropas americanas no Oriente Médio até 2027 e prepara novas rotações de forças para a região.

Apesar disso, Trump reiterou nesta quarta-feira sua avaliação de que o conflito terminará logo após as eleições de meio de mandato. O presidente também afirmou que uma solução diplomática continua sendo possível, embora não seja sua opção preferida.

A Casa Branca não respondeu imediatamente a pedidos de comentário da Reuters sobre as informações divulgadas pelo jornal.

Petróleo e frente saudita ampliam tensão

A tensão também aumentou em outra frente do conflito: os confrontos entre a Arábia Saudita e os rebeldes houthis, grupo apoiado pelo Irã no Iêmen . As autoridades sauditas emitiram novos alertas de emergência na cidade de Khamis Mushait, no sudoeste do país, após uma série de ataques atribuídos aos houthis.

Membros das forças governamentais iemenitas apoiadas pela Arábia Saudita reagem durante o que descrevem como confrontos com os houthis. — Foto: MEDIA CENTRE OF THE YEMENI ARMED

Segundo a coalizão liderada pela Arábia Saudita, ao menos 73 pessoas ficaram feridas em recentes ataques contra cidades do sul saudita. Os houthis afirmaram ter atingido uma base aérea e infraestruturas ligadas ao setor de petróleo na região.

A guerra e a alta dos preços dos combustíveis também têm pressionado a popularidade de Trump, que enfrenta uma eleição de meio de mandato considerada crucial para a continuidade de sua agenda no Congresso.

articles.body:

articles.title: BR-447 no ES será um dos menores trechos de rodovia federal do Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Investimento no trecho de 4,33 quilômetros no Espírito Santo é de R$ 236 milhões. A expectativa, segundo o governo federal, é inaugurar a BR-447 até dezembro deste ano.
articles.summary: Investimento no trecho de 4,33 quilômetros no Espírito Santo é de R$ 236 milhões. A expectativa, segundo o governo federal, é inaugurar a BR-447 até dezembro deste ano.
articles.body:
Início do novo trecho da BR-447, que vai ligar a BR-101 até a Rodovia Leste-Oeste — Foto: Fernando Madeira/Rede Gazeta

Um novo trecho da BR-447 no Espírito Santo deve ser inaugurado até dezembro deste ano, segundo o governo federal. Com 4,3 quilômetros de extensão , a via será um dos menores trechos de rodovia federal de todo o país. O investimento total é de R$ 236 milhões, com recursos da União.

O trecho a ser entregue pelo Departamento Nacional de Infraestrutura de Transportes (Dnit) vai ligar a BR-101, nos limites entre Cariacica e Viana, próximo à antiga Braspérola, até a Rodovia estadual Leste-Oeste, ainda em Cariacica, próximo ao novo Hospital Geral.

A previsão de inauguração para este ano ainda é do ministro dos Transportes, George Santoro, que informou que o governo federal ainda aguarda a saída de sete famílias de áreas de risco, em um processo que envolve desapropriações, para que a via seja concluída.

"Com elas cumprindo o prazo determinado pela Justiça, a gente consegue entregar a rodovia em dezembro deste ano", afirmou Santoro. Ele disse que as desapropriações vão ser pagas pela União, que também vai assumir os valores referentes à realocação dessas famílias.

Trecho da BR-447 que será inaugurado entre a BR-101 até a Rodovia Leste-Oeste — Foto: Reprodução/Entre Praias e Morros/YouTube

Esse novo trecho que será entregue até dezembro (4,3 km) vai complementar um outro já existente da BR-447, em Vila Velha. Conhecida como Estrada de Capuaba, o trecho já em operação atualmente liga a Avenida Carlos Lindenberg até o Porto de Capuaba e tem cerca de dois quilômetros de extensão.

Portanto, somando os dois trechos distintos que a BR-447 terá no Espírito Santo após a inauguração de dezembro, a rodovia federal deve somar 6,4 km de extensão, tornando-se o sexto menor trecho de BR em todo o país. Confira abaixo:

Toda a extensão da nova via será em pista dupla, nos dois sentidos, além de incluir vias marginais e a construção de cinco obras especiais, como viadutos.

Além desses dois trechos distintos, o Dnit informou que, como um todo, a BR-447 deverá ter, oficialmente, 16,3 quilômetros de extensão, "abrangendo tanto o trecho já pavimentado quanto os demais segmentos projetados, inclusive aqueles coincidentes com rodovias estaduais".

Ou seja, o Dnit também vai contabilizar como BR-447 os trechos em que a rodovia federal passa pelo menos trajeto de outras vias locais, como a própria Rodovia Leste-Oeste e a Darly Santos. "Dessa forma, essa quilometragem não se restringe aos trechos atualmente sob jurisdição do Dnit", completou o órgão.

E mesmo com esse tamanho total de 16,3 km, a BR-447 no Espírito Santo ainda assim será umas das menores rodovias federais do Brasil.

A promessa de entrega para dezembro de 2026 é a mesma feita pelo Ministério dos Transportes no início deste ano, após o prazo anterior — conclusão em dezembro de 2025 — não ser cumprida.

Essas não foram as primeiras promessas: em janeiro de 2024, o então ministro dos Transportes, Renan Filho, listou a via no Espírito Santo entre os 60 projetos previstos para serem entregues ou iniciados naquele ano.

Um ano antes, em 2023, a entrega da rodovia também foi anunciada, mas o governo federal só havia liberado 1,2 quilômetro de vias laterais até julho daquele ano, no trecho que liga os bairros São Francisco e Vila Betânia, nos municípios de Cariacica e Viana, respectivamente.

A ordem de serviço para a BR-447 foi em 2019, com previsão inicial de realizar toda a obra em até três anos. Mas, em 2022, o governo federal já explicava o desafio que enfrentava com a desapropriação dos mais de 300 imóveis previstos no projeto.

Quatro anos atrás, ainda era necessário desapropriar 180 imóveis para seguir com a construção da rodovia.

articles.title: Nove estados do Centro-Sul devem ter tempestades nesta quinta | G1
articles.standfirst: Nove estados do Centro-Sul do Brasil têm avisos para chuvas fortes no fim desta semana. Extremo norte do Rio Grande do Sul, centro-oeste de Santa Catarina e do Paraná e extremo sul do Mato Grosso do Sul são as áreas que devem registrar os maiores volumes de chuva.
articles.summary: Nove estados do Centro-Sul do Brasil têm avisos para chuvas fortes no fim desta semana.
articles.body:
chuva paraná vento tempestade temporal vendaval — Foto: Gilson Abreu/AEN

Boa parte do Centro-Sul do Brasil deve seguir com tempo chuvoso nesta quinta-feira (10). Segundo a Climatempo, as instabilidades são provocadas pela combinação de um cavado e de um sistema de baixa pressão no interior da América do Sul.

⛈️ Cavados são áreas alongadas de baixa pressão. Esse fenômeno meteorológico acontece quando há uma corrente de vento que ajuda na formação de nuvens de tempestade .

Com a previsão de chuvas fortes, o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia ( Inmet ) emitiu avisos de tempestades para nove estados para esta quinta:

Segundo o Inmet, o extremo norte do Rio Grande do Sul, centro-oeste de Santa Catarina e do Paraná e extremo sul do Mato Grosso do Sul são as áreas que devem registrar os maiores volumes de chuva. (veja no mapa abaixo)

⚠️Esses locais têm aviso de grande perigo para tempestades nesta quinta, com previsão de mais de 100 milímetros de chuva por dia e ventos superiores a 100 km/h . Também há risco de alagamentos e queda de árvores.

Previsão de tempestades para o Centro-Sul. — Foto: Arte/g1

O tempo instável também pode aumentar o risco da formação de tornados nessa região .

Segundo a Climatempo, nuvens extremamente carregadas devem se configurar em áreas do Paraná, extremo sul do Mato Grosso e sudoeste e sul de São Paulo. (veja no mapa abaixo região que pode ser atingida)

Risco de tornado nesta quinta-feira (10). — Foto: Arte/g1

O fenômeno pode acontecer nesta quinta-feira (10) e também na sexta (11), quando uma nova frente fria vai se aproximar do Sul do país e pode intensificar as instabilidades.

A previsão indica tempo instável em diferentes áreas do país nesta quinta, com chuva forte e risco de temporais no Sul , Sudeste e Centro-Oeste . O Norte também terá pancadas de chuva e calor . No Nordeste , a chuva fica mais concentrada no litoral, e o interior segue seco , com baixa umidade e temperaturas elevadas.

Veja abaixo como fica o tempo em cada região do Brasil:

O Paraná tem previsão de chuva desde cedo, com intensificação dos temporais ao longo do dia. Há risco de raios, ventos de 50 a 70 km/h e acumulados elevados. Há possibilidade de tornados , principalmente no norte e oeste.

Em Santa Catarina , os maiores volumes de chuva são esperados no oeste, planalto norte e regiões próximas à divisa com o Paraná.

Já no Rio Grande do Sul , a chuva fica concentrada na metade norte, enquanto a Campanha Gaúcha e o sul têm tempo mais estável, com possibilidade de chuva fraca e isolada.

As temperaturas ficam amenas durante a manhã em todos os estados, com aumento gradual ao longo do dia. Oeste e norte do Paraná e oeste e noroeste gaúcho devem ter uma tarde mais quente, favorecendo a instabilidade.

São Paulo , Rio de Janeiro e Espírito Santo devem ter chuva desde cedo, com aumento da intensidade à tarde e risco de temporais, trovoadas e ventos de até 70 km/h.

Em Minas Gerais , a previsão é de chuva forte no centro-sul, oeste, leste e Triângulo Mneiro, com maior risco no extremo sul. O norte do estado segue com tempo firme.

Há risco de temporais em todo o estado de São Paulo, no sul de Minas Gerais, no Triângulo Mineiro e no Rio de Janeiro. Há possibilidade de tornados no sul e sudoeste paulista.

As temperaturas ficam mais amenas nas áreas com maior nebulosidade, mas permanecem elevadas nas demais regiões.

Apesar da nebulosidade prevista para a região, o calor deve predominar à tarde em boa parte dos estados do Centro-Oeste, com sensação de tempo abafado.

O Mato Grosso do Sul deve ter pancadas moderadas a fortes, com maior risco de temporais no sul e leste. Há possibilidade de tornados e acumulados elevados de chuva. Os ventos podem chegar a 70 km/h e superar esse valor no sul.

Em Goiás e no Mato Grosso , a previsão é de chuva mais irregular, principalmente no centro-sul e leste de Goiás e no centro-oeste e sul de Mato Grosso. Já o Distrito Federal pode ter pancadas de chuva moderadas a fortes.

No Nordeste, a chuva deve ficar concentrada no litoral da região, enquanto o tempo permanece seco e com baixa umidade no interior.

Há previsão de chuva moderada a forte na Bahia , principalmente entre Salvador, recôncavo baiano e sul do estado.

Também há expectativa de chuva no litoral do Rio Grande do Norte e de Alagoas , além de pancadas isoladas no Ceará e chuva fraca a moderada no Maranhão .

No interior, o predomínio do sol mantém o tempo seco, com baixa umidade e calor. No sul do Piauí , por exemplo, a umidade pode ficar entre 12% e 20%.

No Norte, há previsão de chuva forte e calor para esta quinta-feira. Pancadas moderadas a fortes devem se concentrar em áreas do Amazonas , Roraima , Rondônia e no oeste e sudoeste do Pará . O norte do Amazonas tem risco de temporais.

O tempo fica mais firme no Acre e em parte do Pará . Pontos do centro e oeste do Pará podem ter chuva fraca.

A sensação de abafamento persiste em toda a região. No Tocantins , a umidade pode variar entre 20% e 30%.

articles.title: Moradores do Jaraguá, em Montes Claros, comemoram a chegada do asfalto | G1
articles.standfirst: Pavimentação marca o início de um novo tempo para o bairro.
articles.summary: Pavimentação marca o início de um novo tempo para o bairro.
articles.body:
Com o objetivo de colocar fim a problemas históricos enfrentados pelos moradores, como a poeira nos períodos de estiagem e a lama durante as chuvas, o Município de Montes Claros continua executando seu programa de pavimentação asfáltica, proporcionando mais conforto, segurança e bem-estar para a população, refletindo positivamente na saúde das pessoas.

Para o Seu Benedito, “agora, tudo será melhor” — Foto: Solon Queiroz

Desta vez, quem está comemorando a chegada do asfalto são os moradores da rua Treze, no bairro Jaraguá II. É o caso de Benedito Soares da Silva, que destacou ser “bom demais ver a chegada deste asfalto depois de anos de espera. Agora, tudo será melhor, sem lama e sem poeira”.

“Nosso direito de ir e vir está garantido”, destaca Getúlio Neves, presidente da Associação de Moradores — Foto: Solon Queiroz

"Nosso direito de ir e vir está garantido, pois, antes, até viagens de aplicativos eram canceladas devido aos buracos nesta via. Além disso, tudo melhora com o asfalto. A saúde principalmente, eliminando a poeira e consequentemente as alergias. Sem falar na valorização dos nossos imóveis", afirmou Getúlio Neves, presidente da Associação de Moradores do bairro.

O asfaltamento da rua Treze faz parte de um pacote de pavimentação que inclui os bairros Village do Lago I e Jaraguá I e II, contemplando a pavimentação da avenida Perimetral, da alameda Zaira Celestino Pinheiro e da Alameda das Candeias.

articles.title: História de irmãos mortos sozinhos expõe drama na China; entenda  | G1
articles.standfirst: Quatro crianças foram encontradas mortas após beberem veneno em uma casa onde viviam sozinhas; caso está ligado ao êxodo de trabalhadores rurais que deixou milhões de filhos aos cuidados dos avós.
articles.summary: Quatro crianças foram encontradas mortas após beberem veneno em uma casa onde viviam sozinhas; caso está ligado ao êxodo de trabalhadores rurais que deixou milhões de filhos aos cuidados dos avós.
articles.body:
A história de quatro irmãos mortos dentro de um quarto na China revela um dos lados menos conhecidos do rápido desenvolvimento econômico do país: o custo humano da migração de trabalhadores das áreas rurais para os grandes centros industriais.

O menino mais velho tinha 13 anos. As três irmãs tinham 9, 7 e 5 anos. Os quatro viviam sozinhos e frequentavam a escola, mas não havia nenhum adulto responsável por eles.

As crianças se alimentavam apenas de farinha de milho crua. O pai, que havia deixado a região para trabalhar, enviava o equivalente a R$ 500 por mês. Sem alguém que cuidasse delas, os quatro foram encontrados mortos depois de beberem juntos um frasco de veneno.

O caso aconteceu em uma região rural da China e funcionários do governo foram demitidos após a tragédia. A cidade chegou a ser fechada para a imprensa durante três semanas.

Até hoje, não se sabe qual era o rosto das quatro crianças. O único registro da história é uma fotografia do quarto onde elas viviam.

A tragédia está relacionada a um fenômeno que marcou o crescimento econômico chinês nas últimas décadas: a migração em massa de trabalhadores rurais para outras regiões do país.

Na província de Guizhou, onde fica a ponte mais alta do mundo, cerca de 600 mil pessoas deixavam a região todos os anos para trabalhar principalmente na indústria têxtil. No início desse processo, a reportagem afirma que o salário médio era de US$ 25 por mês.

Os trabalhadores recebiam alojamento e alimentação e enviavam boa parte do dinheiro para suas famílias.

O movimento ajudou a tirar milhões de pessoas da pobreza, mas também separou pais e filhos. Segundo a reportagem, quase 90 milhões de crianças chinesas ficaram para trás durante esse processo e passaram a ser criadas principalmente pelos avós.

Hoje, a China tem cerca de 180 milhões de trabalhadores migrantes rurais, de acordo com o material exibido na reportagem.

Uma das razões para essa separação era o chamado sistema hukou, um registro de residência que, durante décadas, dificultou o acesso dos trabalhadores migrantes e de seus filhos a serviços públicos nas cidades onde eles trabalhavam.

Na prática, famílias originárias de regiões como Guizhou podiam se mudar para trabalhar em fábricas, mas não tinham os mesmos direitos de acesso a serviços urbanos. Os filhos, por exemplo, não podiam simplesmente ser matriculados nas escolas próximas às fábricas.

Isso criou, segundo a reportagem, uma enorme força de trabalho barata, fundamental para o modelo econômico chinês das últimas quatro ou cinco décadas.

Nos últimos anos, o sistema foi flexibilizado. Algumas escolas passaram a aceitar filhos de trabalhadores migrantes, embora ainda existam restrições, como a realização do vestibular no local de origem.

Após casos como o dos quatro irmãos, o governo também passou a adotar medidas de acompanhamento de crianças que vivem sem os pais. Segundo a reportagem, elas passaram a receber mais apoio da polícia e do Ministério da Educação e a ser monitoradas por celular.

Essas medidas teriam contribuído para reduzir o problema.

Ao mesmo tempo, a China tenta mudar a imagem dessas regiões rurais. Guizhou, por exemplo, passou a ser apresentada como um novo destino turístico, com grandes obras de infraestrutura, internet 5G e iniciativas para estimular a economia local.

A reportagem, porém, mostra o contraste entre essa imagem e a realidade de comunidades que perderam parte de sua população para os grandes centros industriais.

A ponte de 625 metros sobre o cânion, símbolo da capacidade chinesa de construir grandes obras em tempo recorde, está justamente em uma dessas regiões.

De um lado, infraestrutura, tecnologia e turismo. Do outro, uma história de crianças que ficaram para trás durante o processo que ajudou a transformar a China em uma potência econômica.

articles.title: El Niño no RJ: Defesa Civil e comitê se preparam para seca e chuvas | G1
articles.standfirst: Força Especializada da Defesa Civil foi criada para atuar em situações de emergência; governo também criou comitê com 18 órgãos para enfrentar impactos do fenômeno.
articles.summary: Com foco no El Niño no Rio de Janeiro, o governo estadual criou uma força da Defesa Civil e um comitê para mitigar riscos de chuvas intensas e seca extrema.
articles.body:
O estado do Rio de Janeiro se prepara para enfrentar possíveis efeitos do El Niño, fenômeno climático que pode alterar os padrões de chuva, temperatura e vento. A previsão dos meteorologistas é de períodos de chuva mais frequentes em setembro e outubro, seguidos por períodos mais secos entre o fim da primavera e o verão. Depois da estiagem, a expectativa é de chuvas mais intensas no verão.

Diante do cenário, o governo do estado reforçou a estrutura de prevenção e resposta a desastres. Uma das medidas foi a criação, no fim do ano passado, da Força Especializada da Defesa Civil, formada por cerca de 200 militares e voltada para a prevenção e atuação em situações de emergência.

A preparação inclui treinamentos para que os agentes estejam aptos a montar bases operacionais em locais atingidos por eventos extremos. Durante uma das simulações, uma estrutura temporária é transformada em um gabinete de crise, onde coordenadores e representantes de órgãos mobilizados acompanham informações para orientar a tomada de decisões.

Um analista monitora imagens e dados em um telão e produz relatórios que servem de base para as autoridades definirem as ações necessárias.

RJ se prepara para efeitos do El Niño, com previsão de períodos de seca e chuvas intensas — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

“Aqui a gente tá simulando uma casa que tá num local isolado, precisando de apoio. O analista faz um relatório, chega na mão da autoridade; a autoridade, com base nas informações produzidas pelo especialista, toma a decisão”, explicou o tenente-coronel Gilvane Dias, oficial da Força Especializada da Defesa Civil.

A estrutura também conta com um superdrone avaliado em cerca de R$ 3 milhões. O equipamento é usado para monitoramento e pode transportar objetos para áreas de difícil acesso.

A possibilidade de períodos mais secos também aumenta a preocupação com incêndios florestais. O risco associado ao cenário levou o governo federal a criar um grupo de especialistas para acompanhar a ocorrência de eventos extremos relacionados ao fenômeno.

Ministérios, institutos de pesquisa e universidades participam do monitoramento. A Sala de Situação para Incêndios Florestais também foi retomada, e o número de brigadistas foi ampliado.

Segundo o Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima, o estado do Rio indicou, no fim de agosto, as áreas consideradas prioritárias para ações de prevenção e combate aos incêndios florestais.

Dois documentos, no entanto, recomendados pelo Comitê Nacional de Manejo Integrado do Fogo ainda não haviam sido apresentados pelo governo do estado. O prazo para o envio terminou em 6 de agosto.

O governo estadual não informou o motivo pelo qual os documentos ainda não foram encaminhados.

Se os períodos secos aumentam a preocupação com incêndios, a previsão de chuvas mais intensas no verão também coloca os municípios em alerta para alagamentos, deslizamentos e outros desastres provocados por temporais.

Uma nota técnica da Secretaria Estadual de Ambiente analisou os riscos em 30 cidades do estado. De acordo com o documento, 83% da área analisada foi classificada como de alta ou média possibilidade de desastres causados por chuvas fortes.

Municípios da Região Serrana, como Nova Friburgo, Petrópolis e Teresópolis, aparecem entre os que apresentam maior risco.

Para tentar integrar as ações de prevenção e resposta, o governo do estado criou, em julho, o Comitê de Enfrentamento aos Efeitos do El Niño. O grupo reúne 18 órgãos e tem como objetivo coordenar medidas entre o estado e os municípios e agilizar a resposta em situações de emergência.

O El Niño ocorre quando as águas do Oceano Pacífico ficam mais quentes do que o normal em uma determinada região. O aquecimento interfere na circulação da atmosfera e pode provocar mudanças nos padrões de chuva, temperatura e ventos em diferentes partes do planeta.

No estado do Rio, os meteorologistas do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) indicam maior frequência de chuvas em setembro e outubro e períodos mais secos entre o fim da primavera e o verão.

A intensidade e os impactos do fenômeno, no entanto, podem variar ao longo dos meses.

articles.title: 'Estou boltando': erro de ortografia revela assassinato na Argentina | G1
articles.standfirst: Irmã recebeu suposta mensagem da vítima e acionou a polícia por desconfiar que alguém estava se passando por ele. Entenda por que trocar 'b' e 'v' em espanhol é mais do que um mero erro de digitação.
articles.summary: Entenda por que trocar 'b' e 'v' em espanhol é mais do que um mero erro de digitação.
articles.body:
Imagem do arquiteto argentino Rodolfo Bassi em rede social — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Um erro de ortografia em uma mensagem mandada pelo WhatApp levou à descoberta de um crime e à prisão de dois suspeitos na Argentina.

A história do assassinato do arquiteto Rodolfo Augusto Bassi , de 61 anos, foi contada pelo jornal argentino "Clarín", de Buenos Aires.

Bassi morava na cidade de Paraná, na província de Entre Ríos, a cerca de 500 km de Buenos Aires, e trabalhava na reforma de apartamentos no último dia 1º.

Naquele dia, Bassi tinha conversado com um casal até por volta das 16h, segundo o "Clarín", e desde então deixou de responder mensagens.

Sua irmã decidiu, então, mandar uma mensagem, e recebeu a resposta:

"Estou boltando de Rosário, Moni. Nos falamos."

O erro de ortografia acendeu nela um alerta. Em espanhol, confundir as letras "b" e "v" não costuma ser um mero erro de digitação: elas não têm diferença fonética. "Rebelar" e "revelar", por exemplo, têm a pronúncia idêntica.

No caso, a palavra "bolviendo", utilizada na mensagem original em espanhol, não existe — mas, se existisse, seria pronunciada da mesma forma que "volviendo" ("voltando", em português). A irmã da vítima intuiu que Rodolfo não cometeria esse erro.

Preocupada, ela formalizou uma denúncia na polícia, que iniciou as buscas pelo arquiteto e rapidamente achou seu corpo.

Os agentes foram nos endereços de diferentes reformas nas quais Bassi estava trabalhando. A procura terminou em um apartamento num complexo habitacional de Paraná.

Ele estava amarrado em uma cadeira num apartamento onde foi encontrada uma faca de cozinha e uma marreta, supostamente utilizadas como armas no crime. O laudo preliminar da autópsia afirma que "o corpo apresentava cortes compatíveis com tortura e uma fratura no crânio causada por um golpe com um objeto contundente", segundo o "Clarín".

Rapidamente, a polícia chegou a dois suspeitos, Carlos Gastón Aguilar, de 48 anos, e Claudio Ramón Inofre, de 52. Ambos trabalhavam em obras para Bassi.

Aguilar se apresentou na delegacia para interrogatório com um carro cuja placa foi filmada por uma câmera de segurança na rua onde o crime ocorreu. Ele negou ter estado no local e alegou que divide o automóvel com outra pessoa que trabalha como motorista de aplicativo. Mesmo assim, foi preso.

Já Inofre foi detido em um microonibus que ia para a província vizinha, Misiones. Ambos estão presos preventivamente e aguardam julgamento.

Nenhum deles possui antecedentes criminais.

A polícia agora trabalha na motivação do crime. Os criminosos roubaram o dinheiro e os pertences da vítima, mas os investigadores desconfiam que o crime pode ter envolvido uma dívida ou vingança, dada a violência empregada.

articles.title: Pastel de pudim: conheça a receita que viralizou no interior de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Além dos sabores inusitados, pastelaria de Pindamonhangaba também oferece pastel de içá, iguaria tradicional do Vale do Paraíba.
articles.summary: A pastelaria de Pindamonhangaba viralizou com o pastel de pudim e oferece mais de 150 sabores inusitados, atraindo turistas interessados em receitas criativas e exóticas.
articles.body:
Pastel e pudim combinam? A mistura pode até parecer diferente, mas em uma pastelaria de Pindamonhangaba , no interior de São Paulo, a receita deu tão certo que fez sucesso nas redes sociais — e, claro, nas vendas.

O produto, segundo a dona da pastelaria, Fabrícia Andrade, sempre esgota. Ela conta que a ideia do pastel de pudim surgiu dentro de casa.

"Um dia eu fiz pudim em casa pra gente comer e falei: 'e se a gente colocar dentro do pastel?'. Meu marido falou que não ia dar certo fritar, mas eu falei pra tentarmos", conta.

O pastel passou por vários testes até a versão oficial. "Eu coloquei o doce de leite, que a gente mesmo cozinha, e uma fatia do pudim dentro da massa. Depois é só fritar e assar separado os mini pudins que vão em cima", explica.

Pastel de pudim viraliza nas redes socias — Foto: Fabrícia Andrade

E não para por aí: o pastel de morango cravejado, "primo" do morango do amor, também é estrela no cardápio em Pindamonhangaba e os vídeos das receitas acumulam quase um milhão de visualizações.

"Pensei: 'vou entrar na onda também, né?'. Tem que aproveitar a trend", disse.

Fabrícia, que é mais conhecida como Bia, conta que as duas opções têm muita saída e costumam sumir rápido da cozinha.

"O de pudim sempre esgota. Tem gente que manda mensagem avisando que vem de longe e pede pra guardar. O morango cravejado esgotou quase todos os dias da semana".

O pastel de pudim e o de morango cravejado custam R$ 25 cada. O g1 já mostrou que o morango cravejado tem feito sucesso e é aposta de confeiteiros do interior de SP. Lembre mais dessa história aqui .

Pastel de morango cravejado, 'primo' do morango do amor — Foto: Fabrícia Andrade

Além dos sabores de pudim e morango cravejado, outro pastel chama a atenção. É o pastel de formiga içá - uma iguaria do Vale do Paraíba.

"Meu esposo prepara o iç com a farofa, aí a gente coloca no pastel já crocantinho, com bacon e queijo. Nós deixamos o içá congelado, pra produzir o ano inteiro", detalha Bia.

O sabor exótico atrai um público fiel. "Vem gente de tudo quanto é lugar. Tem pessoas que ligam para ficar em hotel aqui na cidade só para comer. Eles vêm de Campos do Jordão e descem a serra para vir comer pastel", conta. O preço do pastel de içá é de R$ 28.

articles.title: É possível controlar o pré-diabetes e o diabetes tipo 2 sem medicamentos?  | G1
articles.standfirst: Médico lança livro em que detalha programa com dieta e exercícios voltados para regular o açúcar no sangue.
articles.summary: Médico lança livro em que detalha programa com dieta e exercícios voltados para regular o açúcar no sangue.
articles.body:
Daniel J. Cox é professor de psiquiatria e ciências neurocomportamentais da faculdade de medicina da Universidade da Virgínia, e também portador de diabetes. O que ele conseguiu é digno de atenção: criou um programa, batizado de GEM – Glucose Everyday Matters , o equivalente a Glicose Diária Importa –, que o manteve em remissão nos últimos 15 anos sem a necessidade de medicamentos, insulina, ou dietas para perda de peso. Mas como?

Daniel J. Cox, PhD, autor de livro que ensina como pessoas com pré-diabetes ou diabetes tipo 2 podem controlar sua condição sem perda de peso, insulina ou medicamentos — Foto: UVA Health

No livro que acaba de lançar, A GEM Afor Your Pre- or Type 2 Diabete s , Cox detalha 16 anos de pesquisas e ensaios clínicos com seu método, indicado para pessoas com pré-diabetes ou diabetes tipo 2. O GEM foca em escolhas alimentares que evitem picos de glicose no sangue, associadas a exercícios capazes de reduzir esses índices. O professor costuma dizer que não há escolhas certas ou erradas – a questão é que todas têm consequências: “Se alguém tiver vontade de comer um doce, pode consumir um pedaço pequeno, mas talvez precise fazer uma caminhada logo depois, para evitar que a taxa de açúcar no sangue suba abruptamente.”

Na prática, a obra funciona como um guia de trabalho, com muitas perguntas a serem respondidas e checklists – por exemplo, a pessoa deve anotar o número de passos dados diariamente e se o tipo de atividade física que realizou foi moderado ou vigoroso. O objetivo é nítido: construir um estilo de vida dedicado ao controle contínuo da glicemia. Uma ressalva importante feita pelo próprio autor: é indispensável o acompanhamento de um especialista.

O mais interessante é a lista que deve nortear a dieta. Cox relaciona os alimentos que elevam o nível de glicose no organismo – basicamente, carboidratos – a serem substituídos. Aqui estão eles: arroz, milho, batata, grãos como trigo, aveia, centeio, cevada – e claro, todos os pratos que utilizam esses ingredientes, como pães, bolos, doces, biscoitos e pizzas. Ainda entram no “corte” as frutas com alto teor de carboidratos, como banana ou manga; frutas secas (passas, tâmaras); bebidas adoçadas; guloseimas e condimentos como ketchup, mel e syrup .

Do lado oposto estão os alimentos que ajudam a manter a glicemia estável: frutas da família das berries (morango, mirtilo, amora), abacate, laranja; verduras como espinafre, brócolis, couve-de-bruxelas; legumes como cenoura, couve-flor, abóbora, berinjela; oleaginosas (amendoim, nozes, amêndoas, castanhas); sementes (girassol, abóbora); laticínios sem açúcar; ovos; e carnes magras. A proposta é substituir as porções ricas em carboidratos por outras que não aumentam o nível de glicose. Um exemplo: trocar pão e cereais do café da manhã por um omelete.

De acordo com a Organização Mundial da Saúde, mais de 800 milhões de pessoas em todo o mundo vivem com diabetes. A condição pode levar a doenças cardiovasculares e renais, perda de visão e comprometimento cognitivo. Embora o diabetes tipo 2 seja historicamente mais prevalente após os 45 anos, a incidência tem crescido de forma acelerada entre crianças, adolescentes e jovens adultos.

articles.body: A Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) special agent who investigated child exploitation cases has been indicted on rape, incest and multiple child sex abuse charges involving a juvenile girl in Alabama, authorities said. A Baldwin County grand jury indicted Kent Blacklidge, 43, on charges of first-degree rape, second-degree rape, first-degree sodomy, second-degree sodomy, two counts of first-degree sexual abuse, two counts of second-degree sexual abuse and incest, according to the Spanish Fort Police Department. Police said investigators opened the case Jan. 11 after receiving a report alleging the sexual abuse of a juvenile female. Blacklidge was placed on administrative leave shortly after the investigation began, authorities said. OHIO POLICE CHIEF ARRESTED IN FLORIDA AFTER GRAND JURY HANDS DOWN 70-COUNT CHILD SEX INDICTMENT "It takes an unbelievable amount of courage and strength for a victim of these types of crimes to come forward," Spanish Fort Police Chief John Barber said. Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall said his office is prosecuting the case after the Baldwin County District Attorney's Office recused itself because Blacklidge is a witness in other cases it handles. Marshall said the allegations are especially troubling because Blacklidge's duties with HSI included investigating child exploitation cases and helping educate the public about crimes against children. Authorities said there is one known juvenile victim and no indication of additional victims. Barber declined to discuss further details because of the ongoing case. Blacklidge turned himself in Sept. 5 after investigators contacted his attorney, officials said. articles.title: Cockpit recorder indicates pilot tried to abort landing before deadly plane crash
articles.summary: One of the pilots also made comments about the plane's "excessive speed."
articles.body:
Cockpit voice recordings from inside the Amazon Air cargo plane that overran a Miami runway crashing into a van and leaving five people dead, indicate one of the pilots called for a "go-around" to abort the landing just seconds before the crash.

The NTSB, which is investigating the crash, released a readout of the final minutes before the crash taken from the cockpit voice recorder, which contained more than 2 hours of audio.

About 1 minute and 42 seconds before the plane crashed, one of the pilots warned they were going too fast and continued to make comments about the plane's "excessive speed throughout the remainder of the recording," according to the NTSB summary.

About 30 seconds before the crash, the NTSB said sounds similar to the aircraft touching down can be heard, but about 15 seconds later, one of the pilots called for the "go-around" to abort the landing. Just five seconds later, the plane had already veered off the runway.

The release of the select moments captured on the cockpit voice recordings came the same day the NTSB expected to interview the two pilots, NTSB Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy told reporters at an earlier press briefing.

In its update on Wednesday, the NTSB did not share any information from the pilot interviews.

A preliminary report is expected in the new few weeks.

At the press briefing Tuesday, NTSB officials discussed some of the details recovered from the flight data recorder, which indicated that the plane was coming in for landing, but that several seconds before the recording ends, throttles increased consistent with a "go-around thrust," NTSB investigator Chihoon Shin said. A few seconds later, brakes were reapplied and continued to be applied until the end of the recording, but there was no indication that speed brakes or thrust reversers were deployed, he said.

The cargo plane, Amazon Air Flight 7598 arriving from Puerto Rico, was carrying about 32,000 pounds of mostly contact lenses, Homendy said.

When it overran the runway, the plane hit a Ford Econoline van owned by a company that cleans aircraft, with seven people inside.

The five people who were killed were identified by the Miami-Dade County Sheriff's Office as: Rolando Aleman Leon, 55; Yoel Rodriguez Narajo, 53; Julio C. Pineda, 75; Carlos Acosta Fajardo, 53; and Javierkys Reyes Quevedo, 47.

The aircraft's two pilots were treated and have been released from the hospital, according to the sheriff's office.

articles.title: A Canadian town's famous warm welcome doesn't extend to US ambassador on 9/11 anniversary
articles.summary: Gander, Newfoundland, opened its doors to more than 6,000 stranded air travellers on 9/11. Now they wonder if Trump's representative in Canada belongs at their commemoration.
articles.body:
On 9/11, the small town of Gander, Newfoundland, welcomed thousands of stranded Americans whose flights were redirected after the attacks on the World Trade Centre and the Pentagon.

Twenty-five years later, residents of that very same Atlantic coast community are less enthusiastic about hosting the US ambassador to Canada for commemoration ceremonies on Friday.

Some are even demanding that his invite be rescinded.

The backlash against Ambassador Pete Hoekstra's visit is one tell-tale sign that the US-Canada relationship is at its lowest point in decades, and a barometer of how many Canadians are feeling about their neighbour to the south.

It is a dramatic reversal in public sentiment from the turn of the century, when Canada served as a safe haven for Americans in the immediate aftermath of 9/11, and when Canadian soldiers later fought alongside US troops in Afghanistan.

The furor around Hoekstra's attendance led the town council to release a statement last week explaining that inviting US dignitaries is appropriate protocol.

"We understand why people feel strongly about this," the town said .

"We are proud Canadians, and we understand the frustration and disappointment many Canadians are feeling about the current state of the relationship between Canada and the United States."

It added that its focus is on honouring the 3,000 people who died in the attacks.

The US and Canada have been entangled in a trade war since Donald Trump's return to the White House.

Trade negotiations remain on ice after talks collapsed in late August, and each side has imposed tit-for-tat tariffs.

Fewer than half of Canadians now view the US as a reliable partner, versus 83% who felt that way in 2022, according to June polling by the Pew Research Centre .

Hoekstra had already drawn the ire of many Canadians, who accuse him of undermining the bilateral relationship with his statements, including normalising the Trump administration's "51st state" rhetoric.

He has admitted that he doesn't "understand the emotional reaction" from Canadians to President Donald Trump's 51st state remarks, and made headlines last year for a combative exchange with a Canadian official in Washington.

As of early September, a petition in Canada calling for his expulsion had nearly 270,000 signatures. His office has said they are aware of the petition but have declined further comment.

In 2001, Gander welcomed 38 planes at its small airport, along with passengers and crew from 95 countries stranded in Canada after the US closed its airspace.

For five days, local residents provided free beds, food, medicine and clothing for those grounded during the crisis, with people in need almost doubling the small town's population.

Gander's role in hosting more than 6,000 diverted passengers became the basis for the Tony Award-winning musical Come From Away , which tells the story of how the town's residents famously opened their doors.

The musical became a symbol of the friendship between Canada and the US. Former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau even attended the play on Broadway in 2017, along with Trump's daughter Ivanka and former US ambassador to the UN Nikki Haley.

Thousands of other passengers were diverted to other parts of Canada on 9/11, including Vancouver's international airport.

British Columbia Premier David Eby evoked his province's contributions during those fraught times on Tuesday while unveiling a new border sign vowing Canada "will NEVER be the 51st state. Sorry!".

"After all of the president's bad behaviour, after everything that he's done, if Americans ever had to face the same kind of horrors that they did on 11 September, would Canadians step up in the same way?" Premier Eby said.

Couple stuck in Canada after 9/11 hail kind family

Still, some backlash against Hoesktra in Gander has softened in recent days.

Pam Frampton, a columnist from Newfoundland, wrote in local newspaper The Telegram on Wednesday that, while Hoekstra is a "controversial figure" in Canada, she agreed with the town that its commemoration events are not meant to be political.

"To do anything but welcome the United States' representative in Canada to Gander for the anniversary of 9/11 would have contradicted everything the town has become synonymous with - tolerance, goodness, big-heartedness, unstinting hospitality," Frampton wrote.

In an interview with Canadian broadcaster CBC, Gander Mayor Percy Farwell said his town offered "love and compassion" to those who needed it 25 years ago.

"The humanity of what happened here, I think that rises above the political discussions and all the other saber-rattling," he said. "Hopefully this is a bit bigger than all that."

articles.title: For years, plastic bags were treated as waste; then one Nebraska city tried turning 2 million of them into a road
articles.summary: US News: A road in South Sioux City, Nebraska, looks much like any other stretch of asphalt from behind the wheel. Beneath its surface, though, is material tha.
articles.body: A road in South Sioux City, Nebraska, looks much like any other stretch of asphalt from behind the wheel. Beneath its surface, though, is material that would normally have had a very different fate. In June 2025, crews paved about 4,000 feet of Foundry Road using an asphalt mixture containing shredded plastic bags. Roughly two million bags were processed for the project, turning lightweight waste into part of a working road. The experiment is Nebraska’s first of its kind and is being watched as a practical test of whether discarded plastic can find a useful place in infrastructure. For now, the pavement is doing something ordinary: carrying traffic while an unusual idea is put to the test.A 4,000-foot road section becomes Nebraska’s first plastic-bag pavementAccording to Nebraska Public Media, construction crews laid the material on Foundry Road in June 2025. Shredded plastic bags were incorporated into the asphalt mixture alongside conventional road-building materials before the paving work began.For anyone driving over the completed stretch, there is no obvious visual difference. The plastic is not sitting on the surface or forming a separate layer. It has been processed and incorporated into the paving material.The project covered roughly 4,000 feet of road, making it a relatively small-scale test rather than a citywide change to road construction. Its purpose was to put the approach into practice and provide an opportunity to see how the resulting pavement performs.Turning discarded bags into road materialPlastic shopping and carrier bags can be awkward to recycle through ordinary systems. They are lightweight, easily blown away and can become mixed with other waste. In South Sioux City, the project offered a different destination for some of that material.About two million recycled bags were shredded for the road. Once processed, the plastic became part of the asphalt mixture rather than remaining as loose waste. South Sioux City worked with the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, Dow Chemical Company, Jebro Waste Management, Barkley Asphalt, First Star Recycling and Goodwill of the Great Plains. A grant from the Nebraska Environmental Trust also helped fund the demonstration.The experiment moved from an overseas idea to a Nebraska roadSouth Sioux City City Administrator Lance Hedquist became involved with the project after looking at road-building experiments. Rather than treating those projects simply as something to observe, city officials began considering whether a similar approach could be tested locally. The result was a working section of Foundry Road where the material could be evaluated under ordinary conditions.According to Nebraska Public Media, Hedquist said, "We were watching some innovations that were taking place worldwide and what was happening in other countries was very beneficial.""We're making a good use out of products that are just tossed away and blowing in the environment. So we're using plastic bags in a positive way."The road offers plastic bags a second life inside the pavementThe Foundry Road project also reflects a broader problem with materials that are difficult to keep within conventional recycling systems. A plastic bag may be used for only a short time, but the material itself does not disappear when the shopping is finished.South Sioux City's approach shifts the question from how to dispose of the bags to whether some of them can become an input for infrastructure instead. In this case, the proposed destination was asphalt.The project does not mean millions of plastic bags can simply be added to every road. The material has to be collected, processed and incorporated into a suitable asphalt mix, and the resulting pavement still needs to prove itself over time.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Twist in influencer Manjeet Kaur murder: 1st arrest in case; accused claims she was set ablaze in Sector 34
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: A fortnight after social media influencer Manjeet Kaur succumbed to injuries she sustained after allegedly being kidnapped, tied to a tree.
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: A fortnight after social media influencer Manjeet Kaur succumbed to injuries she sustained after allegedly being kidnapped, tied to a tree and set ablaze near Morinda, Chandigarh Police made the first arrest in the case on Tuesday.The accused, Parminder Singh alias Pinda, a resident of Kapurthala, was arrested late Tuesday night near the Sector 38 motor market by a team from Sector 34 police station.Police produced Pinda before a court on Wednesday and secured a four-day police remand for further questioning.According to police, investigators established Pinda’s presence at the scene through call detail records and tower location data linked to Manjeet’s alleged kidnapping. During interrogation, Pinda allegedly admitted his involvement in the kidnapping but denied any role in setting her on fire.According to the preliminary investigation, Manjeet was allegedly called to Sector 34 on the intervening night of July 3 and 4 by persons known to her. She was allegedly assaulted, forced into a vehicle and taken to a forested area near Morinda in Punjab, where she was tied to a tree and set ablaze.Police said another acquaintance who reached the spot later managed to douse the flames with a blanket. Manjeet was initially taken to a hospital in Morinda before being shifted to a private hospital in Mohali. She was later admitted to PGI, Chandigarh, where she remained under treatment until her death on Aug 26.Police are treating the matter as a “double murder” case as Manjeet was allegedly around seven weeks pregnant at the time of her death.According to investigators, Pinda claimed Manjeet had told him the unborn child was his, a claim he denied. Police are probing the dispute over the pregnancy as a possible motive behind the crime.Manjeet’s mother had earlier expressed suspicion against Pinda and Rinku, another acquaintance of the victim, and both were named in the FIR. Police are also investigating whether the accused attempted to exploit an existing social media rivalry involving one of Manjeet’s acquaintances to mislead investigators and create a false trail.Further investigation is underway, and police are questioning Pinda to establish the sequence of events and determine the roles of other suspects.According to police sources, Pinda claimed during interrogation that Manjeet was not taken to the Morinda forest area and was instead set on fire behind a park in Sector 34 following an argument with Rinku.Sources said the dispute allegedly escalated into a physical altercation, after which Manjeet was taken in a car, assaulted and set ablaze. However, the flames were allegedly extinguished later when the accused feared the consequences. articles.title: Trump vows to be at centre of US midterms: Republican convention takeaways
articles.summary: Trump says, ‘Pretend I’m on the ballot,’ as he rallies Republicans ahead of challenging midterm elections.
articles.body:
Dallas, Texas – United States President Donald Trump has delivered a keynote speech on the first night of the Republican midterm convention , putting himself at the centre of the November vote despite not being on the ballot.

The first-of-its-kind event on Wednesday came as Republicans face a challenging midterm election to hold control of the House of Representatives and Senate. Losing either chamber would represent a major check on Trump’s power.

“When I’m on the ticket, Republicans always do very well,” Trump said to a friendly crowd at the American Airlines Center. “But for some reason, when a president wins… even if he’s a really good or great president, they don’t win the midterms.”

“We’re gonna change that,” he said. “So I’m asking you to pretend that I’m on the ballot.”

Vice President JD Vance was initially set to headline the first night of the convention, an event typically only held during presidential election cycles. No reason was given for the last-minute change. The convention was set to continue into a second night on Thursday.

Trump’s decision to put himself at the centre of the midterm elections by calling for a midterm convention has been seen as a political gambit, particularly as his approval rating has dipped amid the US-Israel war on Iran .

But Trump on Wednesday promised that he would be a major feature in the final stretch of the race, whether Republican candidates like it or not.

He pointed to about 35 of the most competitive races.

“We can win every one of those races,” he said. “But I’m going to every one of those states for congressman and for senators.”

“We are going to have rallies just like this.”

It might not be welcome news for all candidates in tight races, including several who chose to campaign in their own districts rather than attend the Dallas convention.

Some political insiders have warned that too-close an embrace from Trump could backfire, instead mobilising Democrats who have already turned out in droves throughout the primary season.

Trump also went further, pledging a $5,000 “dividend” to all adult citizens if Republicans maintain control of both chambers. It was unclear if the president could legally make good on the claim.

Trump hails war on Iran despite political fallout

The war on Iran, which Trump launched alongside Israel on February 28, has become a major political liability heading into the midterms.

On Wednesday, Brent Crude oil topped more than $100 a barrel for the first time in July as the war ground into its seventh month. Polls have suggested widespread disapproval of the war and its knock-on economic effects.

None of the speakers preceding Trump brought up the conflict, which was only featured in a brief video montage in the official programming.

Trump, however, leaned into his handling of the war, saying the US was “winning” and in control of the Strait of Hormuz, despite Tehran continuing to restrict transit in the arterial waterway.

He restated his desire to rename the strait, through which a fifth of the world’s maritime oil trade travelled before the war, “the Trump strait”.

Trump also floated further escalation, including a potential strike on Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site.

The midterm convention serves as an opportunity to introduce Republican candidates to major donors, according to J Matthew Wilson, a political science professor at Southern Methodist University.

“Texas is the epicentre for a lot of GOP campaign cash,” he said. “It’s really a fundraising hub for Republicans”.

On Wednesday, an array of Republicans in tight races took the stage, including Ken Paxton, the current Texas Attorney General who has trailed in the polls behind Democratic challenger James Talarico.

A Talarico victory would be the first time a Democrat won statewide office in Texas since 1994.

“He is the most radical Democrat in Texas history, but he’s also the most well-funded, and that’s why today, I need your prayers, your votes, and your support,” Paxton said, referring to Talarico, a Presbyterian seminarian.

“If we lose Texas, we lose the common sense revolution. If we lose the common sense revolution, we lose America,” he said.

Trump took particular time to focus on Paxton.

“He may not dress right, he may not talk exactly perfectly, and he may not be the best-looking guy I’ve ever seen,” Trump said, as he hailed Paxton as the “greatest attorney general in America”.

Other candidates featured on Wednesday included Monica de La Cruz, a Republican facing a tight Democratic challenge from musician Bobby Pulido to represent her border district in Texas, Senator Jon Husted, who is running against former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown, and Republican Mike Collins, who is hoping to unseat Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff in Georgia.

Pro-Israel Democrat John Fetterman also made a surprise video appearance to introduce Republican Senator Dave McCormick. Neither Fetterman nor McCormick is up for re-election in November.

Wednesday’s programme underscored the Republican messaging likely to define the final stretch of the midterm race.

Speakers repeatedly praised Trump’s approach to immigration, which has seen the southern border effectively closed in parallel with a mass deportation drive.

Several speakers also focused on tax cuts and other provisions of Trump’s signature tax bill passed last year, the One Big Beautiful Bill.

But the rhetoric largely coalesced around the leftward shift seen during the Democratic primary season, exemplified in victories of candidates like progressive Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and several Democratic Socialist of America (DSA)-aligned candidates.

Speakers throughout the night framed the election as a referendum on “radicals”, “socialists” and “communists”. No candidates currently running in either party self-identify as communists.

Republican Representative Brandon Gill called the vote “mainstream versus the extreme”.

He specifically referenced DSA-aligned candidates Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez in New York. He said Talarico would “hollow out your most deeply held Christian faith and wear it like a skin suit”.

He also condemned El-Sayed’s support from streaming personality Hasan Piker, who was repeatedly referenced throughout the night for his past comments related to the September 11, 2001, attacks. Piker has maintained that the comments were taken out of context.

“There’s another political movement in our country right now that doesn’t believe that America is or ever was great,” he said. “They sometimes call themselves socialists. Some even call themselves communists. But most of them simply go by Democrats.”

The night’s programming resembled a Trump rally more than a party convention, with several of Trump’s most prominent appointees, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent, taking the stage.

Many of those in attendance said they remained true believers in Trump’s message.

“I feel like he has stood and made us more of a power in the world, when before, I think we were almost laughed at,” said Maria Garcia, a 57-year-old supporter who travelled from Boise, Idaho, to Texas for the convention.

“I hope it motivates people to come out and vote, instead of sitting home and doing nothing,” she said.

But despite effusive praise on display for the president on Wednesday, a troubling reality remained for Republicans, according to analysts.

On Monday, the non-partisan Decision Desk HQ political forecast shifted its prediction for control of the Senate to a “pure toss-up”. Democrats remain widely favoured to take control of the House.

In Texas, that reality is particularly stark, according to Evan Roth Smith, a founding partner at Slingshot Strategies, which polls extensively in Texas.

Polls have consistently shown Talarico outperforming Paxton, despite Trump’s May endorsement of Paxton. That means that any Trump bump for the candidate will likely be limited, he predicted.

“We see Paxton trailing and trailing now outside the margin of error,” he told Al Jazeera.

“We now, in our polling – and in other polls that have come out – see Talarico creeping closer and closer to a 50 percent mark, which would mean he has an advantage that is much more durable.”

articles.title: When 19-year-old Neeraj was under the rubble of Delhi’s Satya Niketan PG, his family in Jammu identified him on TV: His father recalls the small detail he saw
articles.summary: A day before the Satya Niketan PG collapsed, 19-year-old Neeraj Bawa called his father in Jammu with news about his second-semester results. “I had ta.
articles.body: A day before the Satya Niketan PG collapsed, 19-year-old Neeraj Bawa called his father in Jammu with news about his second-semester results. “I had talked to him just one day before. Neeraj informed his dad that he had passed the exams. It was their last normal conversation.The following afternoon, Darshan switched on the television at around 3 pm in his Kathua home, and saw images of the building collapse in Delhi's Satya Niketan. Neeraj was studying in the capital and was staying at the PG.Darshan's family began looking closely at the visuals from the rescue operation. It was Neeraj's sister who noticed something familiar on the person being pulled out from the debris- the rakhi on his wrist. That was how the family recognised him. Neeraj had been trapped beneath the collapsed building.He sent his location while trappedNeeraj, a BA student at Motilal Nehru College, had moved to Delhi from Jammu for his education. When the building came down, he managed to remain in contact with friends outside. He called them and shared his live location.His father later showed reporters Neeraj's phone while recounting those moments. The location helped his friends identify where he was trapped and reach the area where rescue teams were working. Neeraj remained under the debris for several hours before he was rescued.What surprised his father was what Neeraj told him afterwards. “I told my son to not fear anymore and he replied saying- ‘Papa, I wasn’t scared inside when this happened,’” Darshan told Newslaundry.For a father hearing this from a son who had just been pulled out from under a collapsed building, the words also offered a glimpse of what Neeraj had managed to do while he was still trapped: stay in contact, share his location and wait.'If you have a strong heart, you can see'Neeraj was taken to AIIMS Delhi with severe injuries and has undergone surgery. His condition remains critical. Darshan said a doctor showed him a photograph of his son after the rescue. “The doctor took a photo of him and showed it to me. He said, ‘If you have a strong heart, you can see. The wounds are deep’” Darshan told India Today.Darshan said Neeraj had suffered severe injuries to both thighs. The family is now waiting at the hospital as doctors continue his treatment.In Neeraj’s family, he has three elder sisters and his father. His mother has passed away. One of his elder sisters, according to the family, has decided that she will not marry until her brother recovers.The boy they recognised from a rakhiThe details of how Neeraj was identified have stayed with the family because there was little else to go by in the first images from the collapse. He was wearing a vest. His face was difficult to recognise. His sister noticed the rakhi.Neeraj was among those rescued from the Satya Niketan PG collapse, which killed seven people and injured five others. The incident took place on September 6 at a five-storey PG building in the area.The collapse has since led to scrutiny of the building and other paying-guest accommodations in the neighbourhood. Police have also arrested the PG operator as the investigation into the incident continues. For Neeraj's family, however, the story remains much more immediate.Right now, they are waiting for the 19-year-old who had called his father to share that he had passed his semester exams- and whose identity, in the chaos of a collapsed building, was first recognised by something as small and personal as the rakhi on his wrist. And they are hoping that the next phone call from the hospital will bring another piece of ordinary news: Neeraj is recovering.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.summary: US News: Two people were killed after a Cessna Skyhawk plane crashed and burst into flames while attempting to land at Montgomery-Gibbs Executive Airport in Sa.
articles.body: Two people were killed after a Cessna Skyhawk plane crashed and burst into flames while attempting to land at Montgomery-Gibbs Executive Airport in San Diego on Monday.Footage recorded after the crash shows the small white plane sitting on the airport taxiway with a severe fire concentrated around the aircraft’s rear area, with flames producing a dense plume of black smoke that stretches across the taxiway.The aircraft itself appears to remain largely intact, while the area around the rear of the plane is heavily engulfed in flames.The aircraft reportedly plunged into the runway at the airport, with eyewitnesses capturing footage of the crash and the intense fire that followed. Witnesses said the flames were so severe that they could not get close to the aircraft.Mauricio Godinez and Melizza Cardiel Godinez were at a nearby hangar when they heard the plane hit the runway. Speaking to ABC 10, Godinez recalled: “We heard this loud boom. She peeks out, she tells me a plane crashed”.“I peek outside, and yes, a plane definitely crashed”.Cardiel said the intensity of the fire prevented them from approaching the aircraft.“The flames was just too much”, Cardiel recalled.“If we would have gotten in there, we would have gotten burned ourselves.”Investigators from the national transportation safety board and the federal aviation administration examined the crash site on Tuesday to determine what caused the accident, according to the New York Post.An initial FAA report said the aircraft crashed while the pilot was attempting to land. The plane's left wing dipped before it “appeared to stall and spun into the ground”, according to the report obtained by ABC 10.Surveillance footage from earlier showed the aircraft appearing to gain elevation before suddenly diving towards the ground at the airport early Monday evening, ABC 10 reported.The identities of the two people killed in the crash have not yet been released.The crash occurred two days after another plane crash in Fresno that killed all four people on board.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader and Rajya Sabha MP P Chidambaram has questioned what India has gained from recent Brics meetings, saying he has not .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader and Rajya Sabha MP P Chidambaram has questioned what India has gained from recent Brics meetings, saying he has not seen any tangible benefits from the last two or three summits.With India set to host the Brics Summit 2026 in Delhi, Chidambaram said the country is part of several major international groupings but questioned whether they had delivered concrete gains for India.“I don't know how many Presidents and how many Prime Ministers are coming. I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results,” Chidambaram told news agency ANI.“In fact, we are part of Brics, we are part of SCO, we are part of G20, and we are part of Quad. What benefits are we getting out of that? I can't see. In the last two or three summits, I didn't see any benefits. Earlier, the Brics Summits resulted in some tangible benefits,” he added.Delhi steps up preparationsChidambaram's remarks came as authorities in the capital intensified preparations for the summit.
